text: Continuous Integration (CI) is a common practice in modern software development. When developers write new code, they regularly add it to a shared project. This triggers automated builds, which means the software is put together without manual effort. As part of the build, the system runs tests to check that everything works correctly. This helps teams catch issues early, before they become serious problems. CI pipelines organise these steps into a clear sequence, so every change goes through the same process. By using CI, teams can find and fix bugs faster, improve code quality, and work together more efficiently.
